title: Attention cacheline alignment experiments
content:
Purpose:
Quick experiments to see whether aligning attention kernels to GPU cacheline boundaries (and related memory-alignment heuristics) reduces tail latency and variance for mixed batch workloads. This started as a hunch after seeing bursty 99.9p spikes on short sequences when flash/paged kernel switching happened mid-request. The goal is to collect simple reproducible data and propose a small heuristic for the kernel selector.

Context / motivation:
- Observed: microbursts where small-seq requests (s=64) get routed to a paged path then abruptly pulled into a larger fused FlashAttention call because of batching. Kernel handoff caused lane mismatches and a 95->99.9 percentile jump (~1.6x).
- Hypothesis: misaligned memory accesses across warp/cacheline boundaries amplify bank conflicts during fused ops, especially for grouped kv-cache merges and when sequence lengths are heterogeneous in a batch. Alignment-aware kernel choice or a cheap prefetch padding might smooth behavior.

Hardware & baseline:
- GPUs: A100-40GB (PCIe), H100-80GB (NVLINK). Primary results on A100; H100 runs used for sanity.
- Model: trimmed 7B transformer variant (12 layers, rotary, per-layer LN), quantized to 4/8-bit for fused kernels lab.
- Workload mixes: 70% short (s=64), 25% mid (s=256), 5% long (s=1024). Throughput ~ 1200 reqs/s steady state on dedicated machine with batching.
- Baseline kernel selection: default heuristic currently chooses flash if (seq_sum_threshold && batch_shape_compatible) else paged. No alignment checks.

Experiment list (quick notes + commands):
1) Cacheline-padding test (no kernel change)
- Idea: pad KV buffers when allocating to force starting addresses to be 128B-aligned for all sequences in a batch.
- Command: run profiler docker image with env var KV_PAD=128. Script: run/workloads/mixed_seq_run --pad-kv 128 --model 7b-quant --gpus 1
- Observations: average p50 token latency unchanged. p99 decreased by ~12% for short sequences; p99.9 decreased 18%. Throughput unchanged.
- Notes: effect stronger when batch contains mix of short+long; pure-short batches show negligible change.

2) Cacheline-offset sweep (0..256 bytes)
- Sweep offsets of cacheline start for KV allocation; sample 5 seeds per offset to avoid luck.
- Result: noticeable valley around 64B and 192B offsets (on A100). Worst around 0B and 128B for our fused kernel implementation. Hypothesis: our kernel's internal staging writes groups of 64B, so aligning to multiples of 64B may create regular bank collisions depending on warp mapping.

3) Fused-op staging stride modulation
- Tweak fused kernel staging stride (small internal param) to see sensitivity with and without padding.
- With default stride, padding produced improvement. With stride set to +16B, padding effect reduced. Indicates interaction between kernel micro-stride and allocation alignment.

4) Prefetch + alignment combined
- Add a tiny intra-request prefetch (nonblocking memcpy of first KV pages) triggered when alignment heuristic fails.
- Result: reduces p99.9 by additional ~6% over padding alone, at cost of ~0.8% throughput drop. Good trade for latency-sensitive SLAs.

Profiling artifacts we collected (high-level):
- nvprof / Nsight export traces showing warp stalls correlating with kernel switch windows.
- perf counters: L2 load/store efficiency drops during handoff; memory controller replay counters spike at misaligned offsets.
- microtraces: queue depth histograms show short sequences are more sensitive to cacheline misalignment because they rely more on fused ops that stage many small loads.

Interpretation:
- Root cause seems to be a combination of (a) fused kernel staging stride interacting with (b) physical allocation offsets across KV buffers aggregated from multiple requests. That creates repeated bank conflicts and memory replay for certain batch compositions.
- Flash vs paged: flash path more sensitive because it assumes contiguous, aligned accesses. Paged path has more relaxed scatter/gather paths and hides some misalignment pain but pays in latency for long sequences.

Short-term mitigations to prototype in runtime (cheap, low-risk):
- Allocate KV slabs with a configurable alignment (default 64B or 128B depending on GPU arch). Expose as server config (kv_alignment_bytes).
- Add a tiny padding policy only when mixed-seq batches detected and estimated flash kernel would be used. Cheap check: if batch contains >1 seq length bucket and mean(seq) < threshold && alignment%stride==bad -> pad.
- Optional prefetch flag for experiments; default off.

Medium-term / research ideas:
- Kernel handshake: before handoff, do a lightweight probe to detect bank pressure (cheap sampling of a microkernel). If high, route to paged path or force alignment shuffle. Needs microbench study to keep overhead low.
- Kernel redesign: make fused staging stride adaptive to allocation alignment (more complex but could eliminate alignment-based worst cases). Would require kernel rewrite and perf validation.
- Batch-aware allocator: when assembling batch, place KV blocks in a placement pattern that minimizes inter-request alignment collisions (possible NP-hard but greedy heuristics likely good enough).

Rejected quick ideas (why):
- Always pad to 256B: reduces p99 but consumes extra memory; not acceptable for dense multi-tenant.
- Disable fusion for mixes: reduces p99 but throughput loss >10% for common workloads.

Open questions / next steps:
- Confirm H100 behavior across many machines (do we see same offsets?). A preliminary H100 run showed similar valley but displaced by 16B offsets. Keep in mind architecture-specific cacheline / bank mapping differences.
- Run with larger model (13B) and with different quantization (int8 vs 4-bit) to validate generality.
- Quick PR: add kv_alignment_bytes config + runtime toggle for pad-on-mixed-batches. Target: small change, canary on a dev pool.
- Follow-up microbench: build a tiny kernel that simulates our staging pattern and sweep hardware addresses to map bank-conflict landscape (instrumentable).

Raw numbers (A100 baseline -> after pad+prefetch):
- p50 token latency: 6.2ms -> 6.3ms (+1.6%)
- p95 token latency: 12.8ms -> 11.3ms (-11.7%)
- p99 token latency: 28.0ms -> 24.8ms (-11.4%)
- p99.9 token latency: 72.4ms -> 58.2ms (-19.6%)
- throughput (reqs/s): 1200 -> 1190 (-0.8%)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally experimental and noisy. The numbers are from early runs — please re-run the mixed workload harness (scripts/mixed_seq_run) with --seed N to reproduce.
- If we like the kv_alignment_bytes approach, I'll draft a small runtime config change and a canary rollout plan for the dev cluster.

Tagged follow-ups:
- @Rishi: can you run the H100 sweep and paste the offset valley?
- @Liam: sanity-check memory allocator changes — what are easiest hooks to set alignment per-allocation in our current CUDA allocator wrappers?
- @Maya: think about monitoring: add alignment flag to trace events so we can query in Console whether batches had alignment padding applied.

End of notes.
